title: An invalidated memory leaves current reads and stays out when an old archive comes back
about: A memory is invalidated. Current reads no longer return it; its history is kept and a historical read before the invalidation still returns it. An archive taken before the invalidation is then imported into the same system. The memory must not become current again.

drafts.cognee: §3.5 current reads exclude invalidated claims; historical reads are explicit; §3.6 imports are explicit about what they keep
drafts.ibm: Invalidate: invalidation timestamp, the record is kept; import makes a new memory in the receiving system
drafts.contextnest: Appendix A.1 rejected is a terminal hide and implementations MUST refuse to publish a rejected document, to prevent silent resurrection
